After completing a $6.4 billion takeover of Australian copper producer OZ Minerals last year, BHP is doubling down on the red metal amid widespread expectations that demand will greatly increase in coming years as the global economy transitions from fossil fuels. 
Solar and wind farms and electric vehicles require more copper than traditional utilities and internal combustion engine automobiles.
"This is the latest move to consolidate in industrial metals driven by a scramble for copper and other metals central to the world’s clean energy movement," Sean Casterline, founder of the investment consulting firm Delta Capital Management, told Benzinga.
BHP, already the world's biggest mining company, is currently the third-largest copper producer behind Chile's state-run Codelco and U.S.-based heavyweight Freeport-McMoRan Inc. (NYSE:FCX). A combination with Anglo American would push BHP to the pole position.  
"In our view, the copper assets are the primary driver of a proposed transaction," RBC Capital Markets analysts said. 
Rival Bids Seem Likely
BHP said it offered 25.08 pounds ($32.27) a share for London-based Anglo American, which said it is reviewing the proposal. The all-share deal values Anglo American at GBP 31.1 billion ($38.9 billion) and is contingent on the U.K. company spinning off its shareholdings in Anglo American Platinum Ltd. description: Anglo American Platinum (Amplats) has cut around 3,700 jobs to reduce spending ahead of a planned demerger from its parent company, Anglo American. Amplats' profit dipped 18% in the first half of 2024, and it declared a dividend of 9.75 rand per share.

title: 23.07.24 Macro Morning - Investing.com Australia
description: The article discusses the overnight market movements, with tech stocks leading the way on Wall Street, European shares rebounding, and the USD moving across the board. Chinese growth concerns and political volatility in the US also impacted markets.

title: Why I decided to sell my Fortescue shares - The Motley Fool Australia
description: The author decided to sell most of their Fortescue shares due to disappointing progress in the company's green energy efforts, which was a key reason for their initial investment. They may consider buying back in if the iron ore price drops or the company refocuses on green energy.

title: BHP stock: Buy, sell, or hold in August 2024? - The Motley Fool Australia
description: BHP Group's shares have hit a 52-week low, but brokers see value in the stock. Morgan Stanley and Morgans have 'hold' and 'add' ratings respectively, citing attractive valuation and potential upside. Goldman Sachs has a 'buy' rating, expecting BHP's copper earnings to increase significantly in FY 2025.

title: Why did the iron ore price just sink below US$100? - The Motley Fool Australia
description: The iron ore price has dropped below US$100 per tonne, which may impact the profitability and share prices of major ASX-listed iron ore producers like BHP, Rio Tinto, and Fortescue. This is due to weaker demand and oversupply in the global iron ore market.

title: Australian Shares Slip After US Market Decline By Kalkine Media - Investing.com Australia
description: Australian shares declined following a drop in US markets, with the S&P/ASX 200 Index falling 0.1%. The energy sector and miners faced losses, while some companies like Pilbara Minerals and Platinum Capital saw share price movements.

title: Anglo to face investors with wary eye on BHP's potential return By Reuters - Investing.com
description: Anglo American investors will closely watch CEO Duncan Wanblad's update on the company's strategy, as they navigate the aftermath of a failed $49 billion takeover bid from rival BHP Group. The focus will be on Anglo's plans to simplify its business and divest assets, while addressing operational challenges that could impact the timing and valuation of these deals.

title: BHP and Lundin Mining to acquire Filo Corp. and form a 50/50 joint venture to progress the Filo del Sol and Josemaria projects
description: BHP and Lundin Mining have agreed to jointly acquire Filo Corp. and form a 50/50 joint venture to develop the Filo del Sol and Josemaria copper projects in Argentina and Chile.

title: Underground Mining Market to Reach $28.5 Billion, Globally, by 2033 at 2.1% CAGR: Allied Market Research
description: The global underground mining market is expected to grow from $23.1 billion in 2023 to $28.5 billion by 2033, driven by increasing demand for metals and minerals and rising industrialization. However, the market growth is restrained by growing demand for renewable energy sources and safety concerns associated with mines.

title: Perseus appoints new Chief Operating Officer
description: Perseus Mining Limited (ASX/TSX:PRU) has appointed Amanda Weir as its new Chief Operating Officer. Weir has over 20 years of experience in the mining industry, including executive roles at Newcrest and Evolution Mining.

title: BHP Xplor Launches Search for Innovators in Critical Minerals Exploration
description: BHP Xplor, a six-month accelerator program focused on critical mineral exploration, has opened applications for its 2025 cohort. The program offers up to $500K in equity-free funding, mentorship, and industry connections to early-stage explorers. BHP aims to tap into a diverse pipeline of exploration projects to enhance its global portfolio and support the transition to a greener future.

title: Sandvik wins SEK 1.9 billion order from BHP for the Jansen Potash Project
description: Sandvik has been awarded a major contract worth approximately SEK 1.9 billion from BHP for the Jansen Potash Project in Canada. The contract includes the supply of potash continuous mining systems, and the delivery is expected to commence in 2028 and conclude in 2029.

title: BHP's Copper Growth Plans Under Review by South Australian Government
description: BHP Group announced that the South Australian government has initiated an assessment of its planned Smelter and Refinery expansion at Olympic Dam. The expansion is expected to significantly increase BHP's copper production in the state by the early 2030s and mid-2030s.

title: G Mining Ventures to Acquire the CentroGold Project from BHP
description: G Mining Ventures Corp. (GMIN) has agreed to acquire the CentroGold Project in Brazil from BHP Group (BHP). The project contains 2.3 million ounces of JORC-compliant gold resources and offers significant exploration upside. GMIN plans to update the resource to NI 43-101 standards and integrate the project into its growth pipeline.

title: Copper M&A Frenzy Masks Greenfield Exploration Weakness: Is AI To Blame?
description: The article discusses the slowdown in greenfield copper exploration projects, with companies increasingly relying on acquisitions instead. Rising costs, long permitting timelines, and geopolitical uncertainties make new developments unattractive. However, AI offers hope by helping identify new opportunities in historical data.

title: New Data Point to Two Types of Mineralization at Property
description: Preliminary results from Vortex Metals' surface sampling program at the Illapel copper project in Chile indicate the presence of high-grade copper, silver, and gold mineralization, suggesting the project's economic viability. The findings confirm the potential for two distinct styles of mineralization - mantos and epithermal vein systems.

title: BHP Tests Caterpillar's New Energy-Saving Technology: Details
description: BHP Group is testing Caterpillar's Dynamic Energy Transfer system to improve the energy efficiency and sustainability of its mining trucks, supporting its goal of achieving net zero operational emissions by 2050.

title: Freeport-McMoRan Sticks With Organic Growth, Takes Advantage Of Geodiversity
description: Freeport-McMoRan is focusing on organic growth and innovation to boost copper production, rather than pursuing costly acquisitions like its peers. The company plans to expand its El Abra mine in Chile and navigate the regulatory environment in Indonesia to maintain its position as a major copper producer.

title: BHP Sees Trend Reversal In Copper Growth, Warns Recycling Won't Be Enough
description: BHP expects global copper demand to grow by 70% to over 50 million tons annually by 2050, driven by energy transition and digital infrastructure. However, the company warns that aging copper mines and complex new projects threaten supply, and recycling may not be enough to meet the growing demand.

title: Teck Announces Appointment of Lyndon Arnall as Executive Vice President and Chief Legal and Sustainability Officer
description: Teck Resources Limited announced the appointment of Lyndon Arnall as Executive Vice President and Chief Legal and Sustainability Officer, effective November 1, 2024. Arnall joins Teck from BHP, where he served as Group General Counsel.

title: After a Nearly 35% Rally, Is This Top Mining Stock Still Worth Buying?
description: Freeport-McMoRan, a major copper producer, has seen its stock price rise 35% in the past year. While copper demand and prices have been strong, recent economic uncertainty has weighed on the market. However, the long-term outlook for copper is bright, driven by trends like electrification and decarbonization. Freeport-McMoRan is well-positioned to capitalize on this growth with its expansion projects and strong financial profile.

title: A $295 Billion Opportunity Is Hiding In Plain Sight. 2 Stocks That Should Help You Plug Into It.
description: The article discusses the growing opportunity in small modular nuclear reactors, which could be a $295 billion market by 2043. It highlights two potential investment opportunities: uranium miner Cameco and small modular reactor manufacturer NuScale Power.

title: BHP Backtracks Its Comments On Abandoning Anglo American Deal
description: BHP has backtracked on its earlier comments about abandoning its $49 billion bid for Anglo American, clarifying that it has not formally withdrawn from the deal. The deal faced hurdles, particularly concerning Anglo's South African assets, and BHP is now focusing on expanding its own operations in South Australia and Chile.

title: Anglo American Offloads $1.1 Billion Coal Stake, Proceeds With Restructuring
description: Anglo American has agreed to sell its 33.3% stake in the Jellinbah Group for $1.1 billion, focusing on copper, iron ore, and crop nutrients as part of its restructuring efforts. The company is also looking to divest its remaining coal assets, aiming to net between $5 billion and $6 billion.

title: Nickel Pellet Market is Expected to Expand at a CAGR of 5.9%, Reaching US$ 3,473.3 Million by 2034 | Fact.MR Report
description: The global nickel pellet market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 5.9% from 2024 to 2034, driven by the increasing demand for stainless steel and electric vehicles. Key players in the market are focusing on expanding production capacity and improving supply chains.

title: Nickel Hydroxycarbonate Market is Projected to Reach US$ 902.7 Million with 5.9% CAGR by 2034 | Fact.MR Report
description: The global nickel hydroxycarbonate market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 5.9% and reach a valuation of US$ 902.7 million by 2034, driven by increasing demand from the battery and electroplating sectors.

title: Legal Storm: BHP Accused Of Sexual Harassment And Discrimination In Australia
description: BHP Group is facing a class action lawsuit in Australia's Federal Court over allegations of sexual harassment and sex discrimination against women who worked at its Australian sites between 2003 and 2024.

title: G Mining Ventures Provides Corporate Update
description: G Mining Ventures has closed the acquisition of the CentroGold Project in Brazil from BHP Group. The project has a significant gold resource that remains open for expansion. The acquisition is expected to be accretive to GMIN's project pipeline.

title: Blockchain in Mining Strategic Intelligence Report 2024 with Focus on Supply Chain Management as the Main Use Case
description: The report discusses the growing importance of blockchain in the mining sector, with supply chain management being the main use case. It highlights the challenges and benefits of blockchain adoption, as well as the market size and growth forecasts.

title: Iron Ore Mining Industry Report 2024: Production is Expected to Increase to 2,605.3MT this Year, a Growth of 2.9% Over 2023 - Global Activity, Exploration and Development Forecasts to 2030
description: The global iron ore mining industry is expected to see a 2.9% increase in production to 2,605.3MT in 2024, driven by growth in major producing countries like China, India, Brazil, and Australia. The industry is forecast to grow at a CAGR of 3% to reach 3,118.9MT by 2030.

title: Iron Ore Mining Market to Reach US$ 829.86 Billion with CAGR of 9.6% by 2034 | Fact.MR Report
description: The global iron ore mining market is expected to grow significantly in the coming years, driven by the increasing demand for steel in various industries such as automotive, construction, and manufacturing. The market is projected to reach a valuation of $829.86 billion by 2034, with East Asia, particularly China, being the dominant region.
